question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. My grandfather B. is not only C. a fastly runner, D. but also a great swimmer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is a fastly runner..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the word 'fastly'. 'Fast' is an adjective as well as an adverb; there is no such word as 'fastly'. The correct form is 'a fast runner'.

• The 'not only ... but also' structure is correct in the sentence; only the adverb/adjective form is wrong.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Some adjectives like fast, hard, late, early function as both adjective and adverb without adding '-ly'. Adding '-ly' to 'fast' is a common error.

• 'Fast' as adverb: He runs fast. 'Hardly' and 'lately' exist but have different meanings (scarcely / recently).

 

NOTE

• Option 1, 2 and 4 are grammatically correct; the parallel correlative 'not only ... but also' is properly used, so the only error is 'fastly'.

question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. He are one of the B. few researchers whom I believe C. has the potential to make a D. significant breakthrough in this field
option_3: has the potential to make a
solution_text:
The correct answer is He are one of the.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject 'He' is singular and takes the singular verb 'is', not the plural 'are'. The correct form is 'He is one of the'.

• Subject-verb agreement is violated in part A.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: A singular subject takes a singular verb. He/She/It → is/was; They/We → are/were.

• In 'one of the + plural noun' structures, the main verb agrees with the subject (He), which is singular.

 

NOTE

• Parts B, C and D are correct; 'whom I believe', 'has the potential to make a' and 'significant breakthrough in this field' contain no grammatical error.

question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The company has been B. experiencing a lot of C. problems since D. the last two years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is problems since.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Since' is used with a point of time (since 2020, since Monday). For a period/duration of time we use 'for'. Here 'the last two years' is a period, so it should be 'problems for the last two years'.

• The error is the wrong preposition 'since' in part C.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: FOR + period of time (for two years, for a week); SINCE + point of time (since 2019, since morning).

• Both are commonly used with the present perfect / present perfect continuous tense.

 

NOTE

• Parts A, B and D are correct; the present perfect continuous 'has been experiencing' is properly formed, and only the preposition 'since' is wrong.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:

The committee arrived _____ a unanimous decision after hours of deliberation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is at.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation is 'arrive at a decision', meaning to reach a decision. Hence 'at' correctly fills the blank.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Collocations: arrive at (a decision/conclusion/place small), arrive in (a country/city). 'Arrive at a decision/conclusion' is standard usage.

• We say 'arrive at a station/small place' but 'arrive in a city/country'.

 

NOTE

• 'in', 'on' and 'into' do not collocate with 'arrived ... a decision' and are therefore incorrect.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: PROVENANCE
solution_text:
The correct answer is Origin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Provenance' means the place of origin or earliest known history of something. Hence its closest synonym is 'Origin'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Provenance (noun): source, origin, birthplace, derivation. Often used for the origin/ownership history of art works and antiques.

• Synonyms: source, root, beginning, lineage.

 

NOTE

• Fabrication (making up/lie), Prediction (forecast) and Imitation (copy) are unrelated in meaning to 'provenance'.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrase:

The manager dismissed the idea outright, calling it _____ without any substantial benefit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is a shot in the dark.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'A shot in the dark' means a wild guess or an attempt made with little chance of success and no real basis. It fits the idea that was dismissed as having no substantial benefit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A shot in the dark = a random guess/attempt with little information.

• Learn related idioms: a stab in the dark (same meaning).

 

NOTE

• A storm in a teacup = a lot of fuss over a trivial matter; A bone of contention = a subject of dispute; A blessing in disguise = something good that seemed bad at first. None fits the context.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: On the same wavelength
option_1: Talking to someone for a long time
option_2: Having similar ideas and understanding each other well
option_3: Waiting for a good opportunity to speak
option_4: Arguing about a different point of view
solution_text:
The correct answer is Having similar ideas and understanding each other well.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom 'on the same wavelength' means two people think in a similar way and understand each other easily.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• On the same wavelength = in agreement/rapport; sharing similar opinions and feelings.

• Usage: 'The two friends are on the same wavelength about most issues.'

 

NOTE

• The other options (talking for a long time, waiting to speak, arguing about a different point of view) do not convey the idiom's meaning.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Disgracers
solution_text:
The correct answer is Honorees.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Disgracers' are those who bring shame or dishonour. Its opposite is 'Honorees' – those who are honoured or given respect.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Disgrace (noun/verb): loss of reputation, shame. Honoree: a person who receives an honour.

• Antonyms of disgrace: honour, respect, esteem, dignity.

 

NOTE

• Outcasts (rejected persons), Rejects (discarded) and Insulters (those who insult) are similar in negative sense, not opposite in meaning.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

Persistent harassment to do something.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Importune.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Importune' means to ask or beg someone persistently and urgently, i.e., persistent harassment to do something. Hence it is the correct one-word substitute.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Importune (verb): to harass with persistent requests/demands.

• Related word: importunate (adj.) = persistent, especially to the point of annoyance.

 

NOTE

• Coerce = force/compel; Convince = make someone believe; Persuade = induce by reasoning. None conveys the sense of persistent harassment.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Sublime
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mediocre.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Sublime' means of very high or lofty quality; grand and inspiring. Its opposite is 'Mediocre', meaning of only ordinary or moderate quality.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Sublime (adj.): magnificent, majestic, elevated, noble.

• Mediocre (adj.): average, second-rate, ordinary.

 

NOTE

• Exalted, Glorious and Supreme are synonyms of 'sublime', not antonyms.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The manuscript will have been translated by the time the expedition returns.
option_1: They will have translated the manuscript by the time the expedition returns.
option_2: The expedition will return by the time they translate the manuscript
option_3: Someone will translate the manuscript by the time the expedition returns
option_4: They have translated the manuscript by the time the expedition returns.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They will have translated the manuscript by the time the expedition returns..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passive 'will have been translated' (future perfect) becomes the active future perfect 'will have translated'. The doer is supplied as 'They', giving 'They will have translated the manuscript by the time the expedition returns.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Future perfect passive: will have been + V3 → Active: subject + will have + V3.

• The subordinate clause 'by the time the expedition returns' stays unchanged.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 changes the meaning; Option 3 retains a vague passive-style 'Someone will translate' with wrong tense; Option 4 uses present perfect 'have translated' instead of future perfect.

question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The ancient manuscript has to be handled with extreme care.
option_1: Extreme care has to handle the ancient manuscript.
option_2: The ancient manuscript is handled with extreme care.
option_3: They have to handle the ancient manuscript with extreme care.
option_4: They must handle the ancient manuscript with extreme care.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They have to handle the ancient manuscript with extreme care..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passive 'has to be handled' converts to the active 'have to handle' with an added subject 'They'. This keeps the same modal-like obligation ('has to/have to') and meaning: 'They have to handle the ancient manuscript with extreme care.'

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Passive: has/have to be + V3 → Active: subject + has/have to + V1.

• When the agent is unknown, a general subject like 'They/One' is supplied.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 makes 'Extreme care' the doer, which is illogical; Option 2 is still passive; Option 4 changes 'have to' to 'must', altering the exact structure.

question: One of these words is spelled incorrectly. Which one is it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Joviel.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Jovial (adj.): cheerful, jolly, good-humoured.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The trend of wearing boots is something that has most sure come around this season."
solution_text:
The correct answer is most certainly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The highlighted 'most sure' (an adjective) is incorrect here; an adverb is needed to modify the verb phrase 'has come around'. 'Most certainly' is the most suitable idiomatic adverbial replacement conveying strong certainty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Adverbs modify verbs; 'certainly/most certainly' is the natural collocation to express definiteness.

• 'Most certainly come around' reads more idiomatically than 'most surely come around' in this context.

 

NOTE

• 'most surely' and 'very certainly' are awkward/less idiomatic here, and 'very sure' keeps the wrong adjective form, so they do not suitably replace the highlighted part.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The head of state will have already addressed the nation about the critical matter.
option_1: The nation will have been addressed about the critical matter by the head of state.
option_2: The nation will be addressed about the critical matter by the head of state
option_3: The nation has been addressed about the critical matter by the head of state.
option_4: The nation will have addressed about the critical matter by the head of state
solution_text:
The correct answer is The nation will have been addressed about the critical matter by the head of state..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active future perfect 'will have addressed' becomes the passive future perfect 'will have been addressed'. The object 'the nation' becomes the subject and the agent 'by the head of state' is added.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Future perfect passive: subject + will have been + V3 + by + agent.

• The adverb 'already' can be omitted/retained without affecting correctness of structure.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 uses simple future ('will be addressed'); Option 3 uses present perfect ('has been'); Option 4 ('will have addressed') is not a correct passive form.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

We are supposed to submit the final report to the department head by the end of the week.
option_1: The final report is supposed to be submitted to the department head by the end of the week by us.
option_2: The final report is to be submitted to the department head by the end of the week by us.
option_3: The final report was supposed to be submitted to the department head by the end of the week
option_4: We were supposed to submit the final report to the department head by the end of the week.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The final report is supposed to be submitted to the department head by the end of the week by us..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'We are supposed to submit' converts to 'The final report is supposed to be submitted ... by us.' The structure 'be supposed to + V1' becomes 'be supposed to be + V3' in the passive, keeping the present tense 'is'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Passive of 'be supposed to + verb': subject(object) + is/are supposed to be + V3 + by + agent.

• The tense of 'be' (is/are) must match the original 'are'.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 drops 'supposed'; Option 3 changes tense to 'was supposed'; Option 4 remains in the active voice.

question:
Read the passage and answer the following questions:

 

In modern households, electrical devices are as common as furniture. From refrigerators and washing machines to smart televisions and microwave ovens, these appliances have transformed domestic life. However, their increasing presence has also heightened the risks, particularly for children, whose natural curiosity often overrides caution.

 

Electrical devices operate on currents that can cause severe injury or even death if mishandled. Young children, unaware of these dangers, may insert fingers or objects into sockets, tug at dangling cords, or attempt to open appliance panels. Such actions can result in shocks, burns, or mechanical harm. Even low voltage devices, if defective or poorly maintained, can be hazardous.

 

The responsibility for preventing accidents rests largely with adults. Installing socket covers, keeping cords out of reach, and unplugging appliances when not in use are basic precautions. More advanced measures include using Residual Current Devices (RCDs), which automatically cut off power during faults, and ensuring all wiring complies with safety standards. Regular inspection of devices is equally critical, as frayed wires or exposed components can turn everyday items into hidden threats.

 

Education plays a vital role. Teaching children the “look, don’t touch” rule, explaining the dangers of electricity in age-appropriate terms, and supervising them around devices are all effective strategies. Safety is not merely a matter of physical barriers but also of fostering awareness.

 

Ultimately, a home equipped with electrical conveniences need not be a danger zone. Through vigilant supervision, proper maintenance, and informed habits, families can enjoy technology while safeguarding their youngest members.

 

"Families can enjoy technology while safeguarding their youngest members."

 

Rewrite the above sentence in passive voice.
option_1: Technology can be enjoyed by families while their youngest members are safeguarded.
option_2: Technology is enjoyed by families while safeguarding their youngest members
option_3: Technology will be enjoyed by families while their youngest members safeguard them.
option_4: Technology has been enjoyed by families while safeguarding their youngest members.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Technology can be enjoyed by families while their youngest members are safeguarded..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active 'families can enjoy technology' becomes 'Technology can be enjoyed by families' (modal passive: can be + V3). The second clause 'safeguarding their youngest members' becomes passive 'their youngest members are safeguarded'. Option 1 correctly makes both parts passive.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Modal passive: can + be + V3.

• Both clauses of the sentence should be transformed into the passive for a complete transformation.

 

NOTE

• Options 2, 3 and 4 either use wrong tenses (is/will/has been) or leave the second clause active, so they are incorrect.

"Education plays a vital role."

 

Change the above sentence into an interrogative sentence without changing its meaning.
option_2: Does education play a vital role?
option_3: Is education playing a vital role?
option_4: Has education played a vital role?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Does education play a vital role?.

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Simple present interrogative: Do/Does + subject + V1 + ...? Singular third-person subject takes 'Does' with the base verb.

• The '-s' of 'plays' shifts to 'Does', so the verb becomes 'play'.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 lacks an auxiliary; Option 3 changes the tense to present continuous; Option 4 changes it to present perfect – all altering the meaning.

solution_text:
The correct answer is Vigilant supervision.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

After realizing their leader had planned to _____ them in the middle of the vast _____, the people refused to follow him any further
solution_text:
The correct answer is desert, desert.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs 'desert' (verb) meaning to abandon; the second blank needs 'desert' (noun) meaning a vast arid region. Both blanks take 'desert', making 'desert, desert' the correct pair.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Desert (verb) = abandon; Desert (noun) = arid sandy region. Dessert (noun) = a sweet dish after a meal.

• These are homographs/homonyms that differ in meaning (and stress in pronunciation).

 

NOTE

• Any option using 'dessert' (a sweet dish) is contextually wrong, so options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect.

question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

Many new ideas are _____ when challenges are bravely _____ by those who dare to think differently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is born, borne.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs 'born' (brought into existence – ideas are born), and the second needs 'borne' (endured/carried – challenges are borne). Hence 'born, borne' fits most suitably.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• 'Born' is used for birth/coming into existence (was born). 'Borne' is the past participle of 'bear' meaning to carry or endure (has borne the burden).

• 'Bourn/bourne' is an archaic word meaning a boundary or a small stream.

 

NOTE

• Options using 'bourn/bourne' or reversing the order (borne, born) do not fit the meaning of the sentence.
